GGIpack2: generic genome interrogation support

Vincent J. Carey, stvjc at channing.harvard.edu

April 06, 2025

GGIpack2.Rmd

Introduction

This package addresses tasks of integrating and interrogating diverse aspects of structural and functional aspects of genomes, with initial focus on the genome of Homo sapiens.

We will show how to integrate information from GTEx (v7) and Ensembl (v75) using resources in this package and in Bioconductor’s annotation facilities.

Use with GTEx version 7 extracts

The following example shows how to obtain a slice of data from GTEx eQTL data relating SNP genotypes to gene expression in whole blood.

The package has an example of data on eQTLs based on RNA-seq analysis of whole blood samples. The example data are 500 records from the GTEx v7 summaries, filtered to keep only SNP loci for which a test of association of rare allele count with some nearby gene had nominal p-value less than 0.05.

Set up database connection and construct the interface

First define the path to a parquet file. The

library(GGIpack2)
blex = system.file("parquet", "testbl.parquet", package="GGIpack2")

Second, set up a duckdb connection to facilitate use of SQL-like querying of the data.

con = DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())

Third, use the GTExresource constructor to create a systematic interface for querying.

wb = GTExresource(con, tisstag="wholebl", pfile=blex)
wb
## GTExresource instance for tissue wholebl
##   coordinates based on hg19
##   num records 500
## table excerpt:
## # Source:   SQL [?? x 13]
## # Database: DuckDB v1.2.0 [vincentcarey@Darwin 24.3.0:R 4.4.2/:memory:]
##   tissue  variant  rsid  molecular_trait_id  score    maf   beta     se seqnames
##   <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>               <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>   
## 1 wholebl chr1_14… rs20… ENSG00000187608    0.0368 0.0127 -0.217 0.104  1       
## 2 wholebl chr1_14… rs20… ENSG00000237973    0.0354 0.0515  0.162 0.0768 1       
## 3 wholebl chr1_14… rs20… ENSG00000227232    0.0487 0.0515 -0.185 0.0938 1       
## # ℹ 4 more variables: ref <chr>, alt <chr>, start <int>, end <int>

A helper method getdb simplifies direct access to the table.

Explore the data and transform a slice to GRanges

We defined GTExresource to ensure that specific fields are available in the table associated with the object.

all(c("score", "seqnames", "start", "end") %in% colnames(getdb(wb)))
## [1] TRUE
getdb(wb) |> group_by(seqnames) |> summarise(n=n())
## # Source:   SQL [?? x 2]
## # Database: DuckDB v1.2.0 [vincentcarey@Darwin 24.3.0:R 4.4.2/:memory:]
##   seqnames     n
##   <chr>    <dbl>
## 1 1          500

That result implies that all the addresses are on chromosome 1. We can assess multiplicities of feature ‘starts’:

getdb(wb) |> group_by(start) |> summarise(n=n()) |> arrange(desc(n))
## # Source:     SQL [?? x 2]
## # Database:   DuckDB v1.2.0 [vincentcarey@Darwin 24.3.0:R 4.4.2/:memory:]
## # Ordered by: desc(n)
##     start     n
##     <int> <dbl>
##  1 126113    12
##  2 115746    11
##  3 109534    10
##  4 139393    10
##  5  88236     9
##  6 135203     9
##  7  88598     9
##  8 591531     8
##  9 602064     8
## 10 632834     8
## # ℹ more rows

To interpret these multiplicities, it is helpful to know which genes (if any) are near the loci that are reported multiple times. Conversion to GRanges is a good first step.

gr1 = toGRanges(getdb(wb) |> dplyr::filter(start %in% c(126113, 115746)))
genome(gr1) = "GRCh37"
gr1[, "molecular_trait_id"]
## GRanges object with 23 ranges and 1 metadata column:
##        seqnames    ranges strand | molecular_trait_id
##           <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> |        <character>
##    [1]        1    126113      * |    ENSG00000238009
##    [2]        1    126113      * |    ENSG00000269981
##    [3]        1    126113      * |    ENSG00000233750
##    [4]        1    126113      * |    ENSG00000177757
##    [5]        1    126113      * |    ENSG00000239906
##    ...      ...       ...    ... .                ...
##   [19]        1    115746      * |    ENSG00000187608
##   [20]        1    115746      * |    ENSG00000238009
##   [21]        1    115746      * |    ENSG00000239906
##   [22]        1    115746      * |    ENSG00000269981
##   [23]        1    115746      * |    ENSG00000268903
##   -------
##   seqinfo: 1 sequence from GRCh37 genome; no seqlengths

Integrate with Ensembl annotation

To learn the gene names and biotypes of the molecular traits identified above, use EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75 (for GRCh37).

library(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75)
g37 = genes(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75)
mults = g37[ gr1$molecular_trait_id ]
dd = as.data.frame(mcols(mults))

datatable(dd)

Finally, close the connection.

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
